opportunities.title: One Stolen Credential, 173 Hacked Tenants: Inside the ConnectWise Supply-Chain Meltdown
opportunities.why_now: ConnectWise just suspended its SaaS backup/security tools after attackers used a single compromised credential to breach 173 Microsoft 365 tenants, and the story is still unfolding across multiple outlets.
opportunities.angle: Timeline explainer: how a single credential cascaded into an MSP supply-chain incident, what ConnectWise customers should do right now, and why RMM/PSA tools remain the softest underbelly of IT.

opportunities.title: BeyondTrust Zero-Day Is the Latest Proof: Your Edge Devices Are the New Perimeter Breach Point
opportunities.why_now: A fresh BeyondTrust Remote Support zero-day is being actively exploited, continuing an unmistakable 2026 pattern of attackers targeting edge/remote-access software over endpoints.
opportunities.angle: Trend roundup connecting BeyondTrust to the year's other edge-bug exploits, with a blunt 'patch cadence' checklist for remote support tools specifically.

opportunities.title: Critical KVM Guest-to-Host Escape Just Rewrote the Cloud Threat Model
opportunities.why_now: A newly rated-critical Linux KVM escape could let a malicious VM break out to the hypervisor, a nightmare scenario for every cloud provider running penguin-powered infrastructure.
opportunities.angle: Technical-but-readable breakdown of why guest-host escapes matter more than typical CVEs, plus a patch-priority call to action for anyone running KVM-based multi-tenant infra.

opportunities.title: Your Router Is Rootable Right Now: The Unpatched Broadcom Wi-Fi Flaw Nobody's Fixing
opportunities.why_now: An unpatched Broadcom Wi-Fi vulnerability lets anyone in radio range get root on affected routers, with no fix yet available — a live, unmitigated consumer/enterprise exposure.
opportunities.angle: Urgent advisory-style post: who's affected, why 'no patch yet' is the scariest phrase in security, and mitigation steps (segment, disable remote admin, watch for vendor advisories).

opportunities.title: Cybercrime Just Got Physical: Hackers Are Now Attacking Building Systems, Not Just Databases
opportunities.why_now: Reports confirm cybercriminals are pivoting from data theft to attacking physical building control systems, signaling ransomware's next terrifying frontier beyond IT.
opportunities.angle: Forward-looking feature on IT/OT convergence risk — frame it as 'the next ransomware payload isn't encryption, it's your elevators and HVAC,' with examples and defensive takeaways for facilities teams.
